references.text: Jacob sets up a stone as a memorial after having a dream in Bethel, illustrating a tradition of raising stones to mark important events or covenants.
Jacob again raises a stone in Bethel as a memorial, this time following God's revelation to him, emphasizing the significance of setting up stones as lasting witnesses.
Jacob sets up a stone over Rachel's grave as a lasting memorial to her.
Joshua sets up a large stone under the oak tree by the Lord's sanctuary as a witness to the covenant, paralleling Jacob's use of stones as covenant witnesses.
Samuel raises a stone and calls it Ebenezer as a memorial to the Lord's help, showing the enduring tradition of raising stones as witnesses.
The verses describe two sides of the same event: Jacob's setting up of the pillar (31:45) and Laban's confirmation of it as a covenant witness (31:51).
